business_problem: Xiamen University wanted a practical way to teach future public-governance professionals how to use and evaluate generative AI, but needed a hands-on environment that could connect theory, prompt design, agent building, and model experimentation for non-computer-science students.
solution_summary: Xiamen University worked with Zhongshu Information Technology and Baidu AI Cloud to build a digital teaching platform for 'AI + public governance.' The platform combines theory modules with hands-on labs so students can move from AI literacy into real model practice instead of learning concepts only from lectures. Baidu contributed the Qianfan Lite platform and Speed model as the technical base of the practical module, allowing faculty and students to work in an authentic large-model environment where they can train models, design prompts, build AI agents, and perform personalized fine-tuning. The broader teaching architecture is designed for public-governance education rather than computer-science specialization: it focuses on responsible AI use, real governance scenarios, and the interdisciplinary skills needed to apply AI in policy and public-service work. That turns the platform into both a teaching tool and a talent-development pipeline for AI-enabled governance.

The outputs feed back into public-governance teaching scenarios so AI experimentation stays linked to real policy and service problems.
